answer: Each agent earns influence by completing randomized tasks for unrelated peers, who cryptographically attest to the result and stake reputation on the review. A new identity starts with no attestations, so it cannot steer high-value decisions; influence grows only after costly, verifiable work across the garden, not by multiplying accounts. A sybil operator must therefore spend real compute and time on each identity and risk losing its stake when peers catch fabricated work, while the vine of attestations spreads only from earned trust, not an ocean of empty accounts.
